mcqQuestions.question: What is the first step to construct a line parallel to line m through point B?

options.text: Draw a perpendicular from B to m
Draw a transversal line through B that intersects m
Copy line m directly through B
Bisect the angle at B

mcqQuestions.explanation: The first step is to draw a transversal — a line through B that crosses line m at a point A. This creates the angle we need to copy.

mcqQuestions.question: Why do we draw arcs of equal radius at both points A and B?

options.text: To measure the length of the transversal
To create congruent triangles for the SSS condition
To find the midpoint of the transversal
To construct a perpendicular bisector

mcqQuestions.explanation: Equal-radius arcs at A and B set up an isosceles triangle at each point. By also transferring the chord, we ensure two triangles are congruent (SSS), guaranteeing equal angles.

mcqQuestions.question: What does 'transferring the chord' accomplish in this construction?

options.text: It makes line n perpendicular to line m
It copies the exact angle a from point A to point B
It bisects the angle at point A
It marks the midpoint of arc at B

mcqQuestions.explanation: Transferring the chord length from the arc at A to the arc at B reproduces the same opening, copying the exact angle a at point B.

mcqQuestions.question: Which geometric principle guarantees that line n is parallel to line m?

options.text: Alternate interior angles are supplementary
Corresponding angles formed by a transversal are equal
Vertically opposite angles are equal
Angles in a triangle add up to 180°

mcqQuestions.explanation: The Corresponding Angles Converse states: if a transversal cuts two lines making equal corresponding angles, those two lines must be parallel.

mcqQuestions.question: In this construction, what tools are needed?

options.text: Ruler and protractor
Only a compass
Unmarked ruler (straightedge) and compass
Set square and ruler

mcqQuestions.explanation: The construction uses only an unmarked straightedge and a compass — no measurement of angles or lengths is needed, making it a pure geometric construction.

description: An interactive tool for constructing a line parallel to a given line through a specified point using the angle-copying method at a transversal. In Learn mode, students view an animated canvas showing each construction step with compass-sweep arc animations and chord transfer visuals. In Practice mode, students answer MCQ questions testing their understanding of the construction method. The tool uses the Singularity design system with Poppins font and purple/orange colour palette.
teaching_notes: This construction reverses the property of parallel lines: instead of measuring angles to check parallelism, we create equal angles to ensure it. The method builds directly on the angle-copying technique from M2.S10.T10. Learn mode features animated compass-sweep arcs showing how each arc is formed progressively. Practice mode uses MCQ questions to assess conceptual understanding without requiring canvas interaction.

tool_objectives.instructions_for_student: Here is line m and point B above it. Our goal: construct a line through B that is parallel to m, using only compass and straightedge.
Draw a transversal line l from B to line m, meeting at point A. Notice the angle a formed between l and m at A. This angle is the key — we will copy it.
Draw equal-radius arcs at both A and B on the transversal. The arc at A captures the angle, and the arc at B prepares the target.
Transfer the chord from the arc at A to the arc at B, just like in the angle-copying construction. This creates the same angle a at point B.
Draw line n through B. Since both lines make equal corresponding angles with transversal l, line n is parallel to line m. The arrow marks confirm parallelism.

instructions_for_student: Construct a line parallel to given line m through point B. The method uses angle copying: draw a transversal, identify the angle at the intersection with m, then copy that exact angle at point B. Equal corresponding angles guarantee the new line is parallel to m.
